preservation: Original24 English weather sources and24 existing isiZulu drafts stay exact. No weather model, threshold, provider request, date identity, quantity formatting or forecast selection changes. Regional copy is bound to the exact English source and template placeholders; updated source retires a draft.2 context-specific error sentences preserve home/report distinction.
layout: Two existing span wrappers contained block-level source paragraphs. They become div wrappers with the same classes/styles; source/quantities remain unchanged. Real browser inspection required. No source-free translated hazards.
terminology: Full native weekday names; no new abbreviations. Source-bound draft wording; no fluent approval. Sesotho sethopo/semelana and weekday orders checked against primary educational sources; Tshivenda weekdays checked against UNISA schedule. Weather-condition terms need further fluent review. Indexed DSAC printedp62/139 distinguish frost maḍaḓa and snow mahaḓa in Tshivenda; Sotho groupp80 supports mohodi. PDF direct fetch timed out: indexed source evidence only, no rendered glossary-page or fluent review. Xitsonga frost uses the indexed DSAC term with an explicit source gloss to distinguish its overloaded snow sense. Fluent comprehension is unverified; no amount/threshold changed.

focused.scope: Weather actual JSX/source copies,36immutableEnglish/isiZulu/unsupported states, real original model/source hashes, all weekday positions, complete warnings/errors/water-null-zero, and no-rain clipping context. Earlier12case set predates observed overflow correction.

verification.scope: Isolated real WeatherWidget with real forecast parser/cache and compiled application CSS. Context-based language provider and synthetic fetch responses; no Auth/consent/account providers. System fallback fonts. Not full Home/Farmer route validation.
verification.remaining: Final ordered tsc/fullnpmtest/diff, pushed draft/CI, native update-note integration and full Home/Farmer route verification; wholeapp work/fluent review remain.

draftRefinements.reason: DSAC printedp62: frost maḍaḓa; gwada belongs to sod, not this warning.
DSAC printedp139 snow mahaḓa: retain its distinct spelling from frost.
Use the same source snow noun with its short-interval qualifier.
Describe fine rain droplets rather than leave an uncertain fog-related noun.
Keep the fine-droplet meaning with plain source-bound wording.
Correct an unsupported noun to plain fine-droplet wording. No rainfall amount invented.

No primary support found for the first proposed noun. DSAC printedp62 explicitly gives gamboko for frost and p139 for snow; retain explicit source gloss (frost) to distinguish the warning rather than invent another term. Fluent comprehension still unverified.
